column1: # Pokémon Scarlet, SDK 13: the same engine build as Pokémon Violet (sdk has Violet's build ID, main the same layout: its allocator setup at the same offset)
# The shader tables, and so the shader translation chain, are Violet's (tables_from): the two games share their engine, and setup maps the player's own dump
# (setup_game.py: shader_map.found.tsv), Scarlet's own models included. The keys the chain hashes (nvn_*, shader_*) must stay equal to Violet's.
# not loaded, main takes nothing from them the host does not supply: subsdk0 (NintendoSDK_movie)
# The NPDM declares 16 MB of system resource (virtual address memory), as Arceus: the game's StandardAllocator reserves its address space in the alias region
# (nninitStartup → StandardAllocator::Initialize aborted with the survey's 256 MB). Arceus' layout: a 5.5 GB block, 4.9 GB of it alias
# Arceus: the pool bounds what the allocator maps
# ---- NVN driver constant segments (the translator's built-in layout, as Arceus and Shield) ----
# the RomFS keeps the shaders as BNSH inside the Trinity packs of arc/data.trpfs (ONEPACK), every file Oodle-compressed: decoded for the split by the game's own
# decoder (dm/host/hle_oodle.c, found in main by its "OodleLZ_Decompress" string), as for Pokémon Legends: Z-A
# shaders the game builds in memory (Shield had 45): saved on the first runs and translated at the next start (Galar Native's capture path)
# Arceus (SDK 11) took the shared font as TTF; SDK 13 decodes the BFTTF itself: left at the default until the first boot says otherwise
# as Violet: Auto picks one tier lower (GameSettings.profile)
# Trinity's open world is heavier than Arceus (about 20 fps docked on the Galaxy S25+): handheld mode, the game's own lower render resolution
